# Hackathon judging (strict): would this write-up hold up in front of the judges?
# Inputs per entry: -i entry=<name>.md -i facts=<name>.facts.json   (compare: one subject per entry)
#
# Where the criteria come from (researched 2026-11-07; event rule pages and organiser guides, see README.md):
#   - Judging criteria vary by event, but the recurring ones are potential impact, technical implementation (does it
#     work, is it sound) and the quality / originality of the idea (Devpost rule pages; one common split is technical
#     40%, idea 30%, design 20%, wow 10%).
#   - Misrepresenting the project is disqualifying. A write-up that claims users, results or accuracy the team doesn't
#     have scores 0.
#   - MLH-style rules: judges consider only what was built during the event, so say what existed before (code,
#     libraries, hardware); credit AI tools, or be disqualified; the code must be public and linked.
#   - Submissions need a demo: a short video (often 2 to 5 minutes, sometimes 2 at most) or a live demo.
#   - Organiser guides: open with what it does and for whom; judges prefer entries that are complete and easy to
#     evaluate, honest about what is unfinished.
#
# Scoring: an overclaim scores 0. Past that gate the entry earns 1/7 of its quality score, plus 1/7 for each of the six
# submission checks it passes.
name: Hackathon judging (strict)
version: "2"
description: Would this write-up hold up in front of the judges, given what is true about the project?
context: |
  You judge one hackathon entry from its write-up. facts.json lists everything true about the project; the write-up may
  claim nothing beyond it. Be strict: when in doubt, judge it as failing. Each check looks only at the kind of problem
  it names; ignore other kinds of problems when judging it.
language: en
scale: { type: numeric, min: 1, max: 5 }
judges:
  jev: { type: decision, provider: typesafe, model: jev-latest }
  clef: { type: decision, provider: cloudflare, model: "@cf/cloudflare/clef" }
defaultJudge: { type: ref, ref: jev }

criteria:
  # ---------- quality: how many points the entry can earn ----------
  - id: impact
    name: Potential impact
    weight: 3
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: minor, description: "A small convenience; the write-up doesn't say who has the problem or why it matters" }
      - { value: 3, label: useful, description: "A real problem for a named group, but the stakes or the evidence are thin" }
      - { value: 5, label: major, description: "A serious problem for a clearly named group, with what was actually shown about it" }
  - id: technical
    name: Technical implementation
    weight: 2
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: unclear, description: "Buzzwords instead of a build; you can't tell what was made or whether it works" }
      - { value: 3, label: partial, description: "A working core is described, but how it works or what was tested is vague" }
      - { value: 5, label: solid, description: "Says what was built, with what, and what was tested end to end" }
  - id: originality
    name: Originality
    weight: 1
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: familiar, description: "Works like products people already use, and the write-up doesn't say what is different" }
      - { value: 3, label: fresh_angle, description: "A familiar idea; the write-up hints at what is different but doesn't compare it with what exists" }
      - { value: 5, label: new, description: "Says what existing options miss, and does something they don't for this group" }

  # ---------- gate: an overclaim scores 0 ----------
  - id: honest
    name: Claims nothing beyond the facts
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [overclaims, honest] }
    anchors:
      overclaims: "The write-up claims users, deployments, accuracy, predictions or results that facts.json doesn't contain (for example a percentage, a number of places or people, or AI the project doesn't have)"
      honest: "Every claim about users, deployments, accuracy and results is in facts.json. Missing sections are judged elsewhere"

  # ---------- submission checks: each one passed adds 1/7 of the quality score ----------
  - id: what_for_whom
    name: Opens with what it does and for whom
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, present] }
    anchors: { missing: "The opening is a slogan or a vision, or doesn't name who the project is for", present: "The first paragraph says plainly what the project does and names who it is for" }
  - id: built_during
    name: Says what was built at the event and what existed before
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, present] }
    anchors: { missing: "The write-up doesn't separate what the team built during the hackathon from what already existed (code, libraries, hardware)", present: "The write-up lists what was built during the hackathon and names what existed before" }
  - id: ai_credited
    name: Credits the AI tools it used
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, credited] }
    anchors: { missing: "facts.json lists an AI tool the team used to build the project, and the write-up doesn't name it and what it was used for", credited: "Every AI tool listed in facts.json is named in the write-up with what it was used for" }
  - id: demo
    name: Links a demo
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, linked] }
    anchors: { missing: "No link to a demo video or a live demo", linked: "Links the demo video or live demo from facts.json" }
  - id: code
    name: Links the code
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, linked] }
    anchors: { missing: "No link to the source code", linked: "Links the public repository from facts.json" }
  - id: limits
    name: Says what doesn't work yet
    weight: 0
    judge: { type: ref, ref: clef }
    inputs: [entry, facts]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, stated] }
    anchors: { missing: "The write-up doesn't say what is unfinished or doesn't work yet", stated: "The write-up names what is unfinished or doesn't work yet, as listed in facts.json" }

aggregation:
  method: formula
  formula: "honest_n < 0.5 ? 0 : (impact_n * 3 + technical_n * 2 + originality_n) / 6 * (1 + what_for_whom_n + built_during_n + ai_credited_n + demo_n + code_n + limits_n) / 7"
  normalize: [0, 100]
  precision: 0
  gates:
    - { criterion: honest, min: 1, message: "Claims users, results or accuracy the project doesn't have" }
  grades: [{ label: finalist, min: 80 }, { label: contender, min: 50 }, { label: out, min: 0 }]
  passThreshold: 80
